newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai B shares inched up at midday on Thursday on speculative buying ahead of the morning close after falling slightly earlier on continued rumours of impending clampdown measures, brokers said.
The B index edged up 0.113 points or 0.13 percent to 87.624 points, off a morning low of 86.624 points.
Volume was 9.466 million shares worth $7.062 million.
Rumours said major institutions would be punished for irregularities and some senior securities officials would be moved, brokers said.
"Bargain-hunting started a slight rebound, but market sentiment is still cautious on clampdown rumours," one broker said.
"Upward potential will be limited with investor confidence being hurt after yesterday's plunge," another broker said. "The index is likely to test the 87-point support level in the short term."
Of 43 B shares, 38 traded, with 17 up, six flat and 15 down.
Huangshan Tourism Development 900942.SS was the star on institutional support, jumping $0.070 or 7.95 percent to $0.950 on volume of 313,300 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded on profit-taking, down $0.010 or 0.70 percent to $1.416 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index staged a technical rebound on institutional support buying in selective stocks, but follow-up buying was not active on cautious sentiment, brokers said.
The index moved up 14.685 points or 1.02 percent to 1,457.202 points on volume of 287.2 million shares worth 4.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index put on 38.443 points or 0.97 percent to 3,990.948 points.
Beijing Lightbus was the star on speculative buying, surging 0.61 yuan or 10.00 percent to 6.71 yuan on volume of 1.3 million shares.
